newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Cyclone death toll in Papua New Guinea rises to six.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone death toll in Papua New Guinea rises to six.

text.p: The confirmed death toll from a cyclone which hit the south east of Papua New Guinea earlier this week has risen to six, officials said on Thursday.
Twenty one people were still reported to be missing at sea after gale force winds and rough seas generated by Cyclone Justin battered the south Pacific nation.
Thousands more people may have lost their homes in the storm, Leith Anderson, head of Papua New Guinea's National Disaster and Emergency Services, told Reuters.
The cyclone, downgraded on Wednesday to a category one storm, the lowest intensity on a five-point scale, was centred in the Coral Sea off Australia's north-east coast on Thursday.
Although hovering about 850 km (530 miles) south-east of Papua New Guinea capital Port Moresby, the storm was strong enough to have caused widespread damage in recent days.
The dead include three people killed by falling trees, two drowned in a barge accident and one who was electrocuted.
Anderson said the death toll could rise, although the situation was unclear because of poor communications.
Reports from New Britain island said 11 people in one boat had gone missing west of the island and another with 10 people aboard had gone missing off the island's east coast.
"I am trying to confirm the 21 people are still missing, but it's hard at the moment to get in touch with the outer islands to see whether people are sheltering there," Anderson said.
"The weather is awful and may take another two or three days to ease," he said.
Cyclone Justin, stretching over an area of about 1,000 sq km (400 square miles), was stationary about 650 km (400 miles) east of the north-east coast of Australia on Thursday.
The cyclone, the largest to appear along Australia's east coast for 20 years, is weakening with winds at its epicentre of up to 80 km (50 miles) per hour, a weather bureau spokesman said.
